breaches.name: Suno
breaches.title: Suno

Phone numbers were also present where they had been used as the sign-up method. breaches.title: Under Armour

In January 2026, customer data from the incident was published publicly on a popular hacking forum, including 72M email addresses. breaches.title: Synthient Credential Stuffing Threat Data

Comprised of email addresses and passwords from previous data breaches, these lists are used by attackers to compromise other, unrelated accounts of victims who have reused their passwords. breaches.name: 1win
breaches.title: 1win
breaches.summary: In November 2024, the online betting platform 1win suffered a data breach that exposed 96M users. The exposed data included email and IP addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, country and SHA-256 password hashes.

breaches.name: TelegramCombolists
breaches.title: Combolists Posted to Telegram
breaches.summary: In May 2024, 2B rows of data with 361M unique email addresses were collated from malicious Telegram channels. The data contained 122GB across 1.7k files with email addresses, usernames, passwords and in many cases, the website they were entered into. The data appears to have been sourced from a combination of existing combolists and info stealer malware.

breaches.name: Eye4Fraud
breaches.title: Eye4Fraud
breaches.summary: In February 2023, data alleged to have been taken from the fraud protection service Eye4Fraud was listed for sale on a popular hacking forum. breaches.name: RailYatri
breaches.title: RailYatri
breaches.summary: In December 2022, India’s government-approved online travel agency RailYatri suffered a data breach. The incident impacted over 31M customers and exposed 23M unique email addresses. Also impacted were names, genders, phone numbers and tickets purchased, including travel information and fares.

breaches.name: Mangatoon
breaches.title: Mangatoon
breaches.summary: In May 2022, the Hong Kong based Manga service Mangatoon suffered a data breach that exposed 23M subscriber records. The breach exposed names, email addresses, genders, social media account identities, auth tokens from social logins and passwords stored as salted MD5 hashes. Mangatoon did not respond to multiple attempts to make contact regarding the breach.
